working_title: The hidden machine behind every swipe
mechanism_question: When you swipe $100, how does that money flow out to the merchant, the card network, and your bank?
payoff: A card earns from a swipe fee on the merchant, interest when you carry a balance, and late fees — map the $100 flow and the one move (pay in full) that shuts it off.

working_title: If it's free, you're the product
mechanism_question: When an app is free, how does money flow from advertisers (and your data) instead of from you?
payoff: Map the flow: advertisers pay the app for your attention and data — you're the inventory, not the customer.

working_title: Selling peace of mind at a markup
mechanism_question: How does premium money flow from many policyholders into a pool that pays the few who claim — plus profit?
payoff: Premiums flow in from everyone, claims flow out to a few; the gap plus investment income is the profit.

working_title: The only game where the house prints money
mechanism_question: When a state sells $100 in tickets, how does that money flow into prizes, overhead, and the house's guaranteed cut?
payoff: Trace $100 of tickets into a smaller prize pool — the expected-value flow guarantees the operator wins.

working_title: The present that sometimes pays the store twice
mechanism_question: How does a gift card hand the store cash today and sometimes keep a slice forever through breakage?
payoff: Money flows in at purchase; some never flows back out (breakage) — free float plus unspent balances.

working_title: Zero interest, so who pays?
mechanism_question: If BNPL is interest-free to you, how does the money flow from the merchant's fee to the lender?
payoff: The merchant pays a fee for more sales; map the flow to see who really funds your four payments.

working_title: They're betting you won't come
mechanism_question: How does a gym's money flow depend on far more members paying than ever showing up?
payoff: Membership dues flow in from many who rarely visit — the no-show flow is the whole business model.

working_title: The currency the company prints
mechanism_question: How do points let a business take your cash now and defer a cheaper reward flow later — if you redeem at all?
payoff: Points are a liability the company controls: cash flows in now, a discounted (or expired) reward flows out later.

working_title: The $35 that appears from nowhere
mechanism_question: When an ATM charges $3 and an overdraft costs $35, where does each fee flow and who keeps it?
payoff: Follow a $3 ATM surcharge and a $35 overdraft from your account to the machine owner and your bank — tiny events, huge per-dollar cost.

working_title: Why boring usually beats brilliant
mechanism_question: How does the fee-and-return flow of a broad index fund stack up against paying to pick stocks?
payoff: Low-fee index funds keep more of the market's return flowing to you; most pickers lose to fees and odds.

working_title: The eighth wonder, in dollars
mechanism_question: How does reinvested interest route a growing flow back onto itself year after year?
payoff: Interest earns interest — a compounding flow where small, early money outgrows big, late money.

working_title: Your dollar is leaking
mechanism_question: How does inflation quietly route purchasing power out of cash sitting still?
payoff: At 3% a year the real value flow of idle cash erodes — a counter ticking down on money that doesn't grow.

working_title: Why your savings pays almost nothing
mechanism_question: Where does the money flow when a bank pays you 0.5% on deposits and lends it out at 7%?
payoff: Banks earn the spread: deposits flow in cheap and out as loans dear — trace the gap that pays for the whole branch.

working_title: You buy the house twice
mechanism_question: Over 30 years, how does your monthly payment flow split between principal to the seller and interest to the bank?
payoff: Early payments flow almost entirely to interest — a flow diagram of principal vs interest shows why you pay for the house nearly twice.

working_title: The house edge, one bet at a time
mechanism_question: How does a tiny per-bet edge flow into a guaranteed casino profit over millions of spins?
payoff: A 2–5% edge on each wager flows to the house and compounds with volume — the math that builds the strip.

working_title: The math of a $15 subscription
mechanism_question: How does a flat monthly fee flow to cover content costs across millions of light and heavy viewers?
payoff: Averaging revenue flow across all subscribers funds the catalog — a few hits carry the whole library.

working_title: Free today, charged on day 31
mechanism_question: How does a free trial route a recurring charge flow the moment you forget to cancel?
payoff: The trial banks on inertia — the money flow starts automatically when you don't opt out.

working_title: A 400% APR in friendly packaging
mechanism_question: How does a two-week fee flow translate into a crushing annualized interest flow when rolled over?
payoff: A small flat fee, rolled over repeatedly, routes a staggering effective-interest flow to the lender.

working_title: Leaving the match is leaving a raise
mechanism_question: How does an employer match route an instant 50–100% flow onto every dollar you contribute?
payoff: A match flows free money into your account the moment you contribute — skipping it forfeits a guaranteed return.

working_title: The real money isn't the car
mechanism_question: Where does a dealer's profit flow really come from — the sale, the financing, or the service bay?
payoff: Thin margins on the car; the bigger flow comes from financing markups and the service department.

working_title: Paying forever by paying the minimum
mechanism_question: How does paying only the minimum route most of your money into an interest flow, barely touching the balance?
payoff: Minimums keep the balance high so interest keeps flowing — a small debt can take decades to clear.

working_title: Three digits, thousands of dollars
mechanism_question: How does a credit score change the flow of interest you pay a lender over a loan's life?
payoff: A lower score routes far more of every payment into interest — same house, same car, very different total flow out of your pocket.

working_title: Buying the dips without trying
mechanism_question: How does investing a fixed amount on a schedule smooth the flow of your average purchase price?
payoff: Steady buying routes more shares in when prices are low — a flow that tames timing risk.

working_title: The 1% that costs you a fortune
mechanism_question: How does a small annual fee route a surprisingly large flow out of your returns over decades?
payoff: A 1% expense ratio compounds against you — trace the flow to see it eat a third of a lifetime of gains.

working_title: The upsell at the register
mechanism_question: How does an extended warranty route a high-margin flow to the seller on something rarely claimed?
payoff: Most warranties are never used — premiums flow to profit far more than claims flow out.

working_title: Cheap handle, expensive refills
mechanism_question: How does selling the base cheap route the real profit flow into the locked-in refills?
payoff: Give away the razor, profit on blades — the recurring refill flow is where the money is.

working_title: Why the deal-hunter pays less
mechanism_question: How do coupons let a store route a lower price to bargain-hunters while full-price flows from everyone else?
payoff: Coupons split customers by effort so more total money flows in — price discrimination in disguise.

working_title: Why the ride doubles in the rain
mechanism_question: How does surge pricing redirect the money flow to pull more drivers onto the road at peak demand?
payoff: Higher prices flow a bigger cut to drivers to rebalance supply — a real-time flow between riders, platform, and drivers.

working_title: The interest you don't notice you're missing
mechanism_question: Where does the money flow when your bank lends your balance and hands you a sliver of the return?
payoff: The deposit→loan→interest flow shows how the bank keeps most of what your money earns.

working_title: The couch that costs three couches
mechanism_question: How does rent-to-own route weekly payments into a total flow far above the cash price?
payoff: Low weekly payments mask a total flow that can triple the item's price — convenience at a brutal rate.

working_title: Why two people pay different prices for the same loan
mechanism_question: How does a bank build your rate from its cost of money plus a risk margin that flows to its profit?
payoff: Your rate = the bank's funding cost + a risk premium — a flow from the Fed to the bank to you.

working_title: A dollar for a 30-cent can
mechanism_question: Where does the money flow between the product, the location owner, and the machine operator?
payoff: A convenience markup flows a profit to the operator and a cut to the location — small sales, fat margins.

working_title: The loyalty program is worth more than the planes
mechanism_question: How does an airline sell miles to banks, routing a profit flow bigger than flying passengers?
payoff: Banks buy miles in bulk to give as card rewards — that money flow can out-earn the seats themselves.

working_title: Getting paid to own a slice
mechanism_question: How does a company route a share of its profit flow to shareholders as dividends?
payoff: Profits flow out as per-share cash — a direct payout flow from the business to your account.

working_title: Set to renew, designed to forget
mechanism_question: How does auto-renewal route a silent yearly flow from customers who meant to cancel?
payoff: Default renewal routes a recurring flow unless you act — the forgetting is the business.

working_title: How $100 becomes $900
mechanism_question: How does one deposit flow through a banking system that re-lends most of it again and again?
payoff: A single $100 deposit spawns a chain of loans and new deposits — the money-multiplier flow that expands the money supply.

working_title: Nobody ships for free
mechanism_question: How is the shipping cost folded into the product price so the money still flows to the carrier?
payoff: 'Free' shipping just reroutes the carrier's cost into the sticker price — the flow is hidden, not gone.

working_title: Pennies per item, millions of items
mechanism_question: How does a razor-thin margin flow into real profit through enormous volume and supplier deals?
payoff: 1–3% per item flows to profit only at huge scale — volume and vendor payments carry the store.

working_title: Shrinking the pie to grow your slice
mechanism_question: How does a buyback route cash out of the company to raise each remaining share's claim on future flow?
payoff: Buying back shares routes cash to exiting owners and lifts everyone else's share of future earnings flow.

working_title: The $29 room that costs $59
mechanism_question: How do fees added at the last step route an extra flow after the price hooked you?
payoff: A low headline price plus drip fees routes more total money once you're committed to checkout.

working_title: One rate, every price of money
mechanism_question: How does a central-bank rate change flow down into your card, mortgage, and savings rates?
payoff: Trace the rate from the central bank to banks to your loans — why a hike reaches your statement within months.

working_title: Why buying more costs less per unit
mechanism_question: How does selling in volume change the flow of fixed costs per unit into a lower price and more total profit?
payoff: Spreading fixed costs over more units lets price drop while total profit flow rises.

working_title: The printer is nearly free, the ink isn't
mechanism_question: How does a cheap printer set up a high-margin ink flow for years afterward?
payoff: The hardware is a loss leader; ink cartridges carry the ongoing profit flow.

working_title: Lending money for a fixed flow
mechanism_question: How does a bond route a predictable interest flow to you in exchange for lending the issuer money?
payoff: You lend; coupons flow back on a schedule, then your principal returns at maturity.

working_title: Easy to join, hard to leave
mechanism_question: How does a hard-to-cancel contract route extra months of dues flow after you've quit?
payoff: Cancellation hoops keep the dues flowing — friction by design routes money past your last workout.

working_title: The payment that never shrinks the debt
mechanism_question: Where does every dollar flow when a loan payment covers interest only and touches no principal?
payoff: With interest-only payments the balance never falls — the flow is 100% to the lender until the term flips.

working_title: Why water costs $5 past security
mechanism_question: How does a captive location route a premium flow from travelers who can't shop elsewhere?
payoff: No competition inside security means extra margin flows to vendors and the airport that leases them space.

working_title: Sold at a loss, on purpose
mechanism_question: How does pricing one item below cost route a bigger total basket flow to the store?
payoff: A loss on the doorbuster is repaid by the full-margin items that flow into the same cart.

working_title: What a share is really worth
mechanism_question: How does the flow of expected future earnings get discounted into a share price today?
payoff: A price is the market's bet on future profit flow, discounted to now — why news moves it.

working_title: 'Protection' that costs $35
mechanism_question: How does opting into overdraft 'protection' route a fee flow instead of a declined card?
payoff: Protection reframes a $35 fee flow as a service — the charge, not the decline, is the product.

working_title: Small payments now, a cliff later
mechanism_question: How does a balloon loan keep early payments low by pushing a huge lump-sum flow to the end?
payoff: Low payments defer principal into one giant final flow — cheap monthly, dangerous at the finish line.

working_title: Getting paid to give you money back
mechanism_question: If an app pays you cashback, how does a bigger commission flow to it from the merchant first?
payoff: The merchant pays the app a referral fee; part flows back to you, the rest is profit — map the three-party flow.

working_title: Free for most, premium for the few
mechanism_question: How does a free tier route a profit flow from the small share who upgrade?
payoff: The free tier is marketing; the money flow comes from the minority who hit a limit and pay.

working_title: Death by a thousand basis points
mechanism_question: How do layered mutual-fund fees route a steady flow out of your balance each year?
payoff: Management and hidden fees skim an annual flow that compounds against your returns.

working_title: Borrow against your car, risk losing it
mechanism_question: How does a title loan route high-interest flow and your car's title to the lender as collateral?
payoff: Fast cash routes steep interest out and your car's title in — miss payments and the vehicle flows away.

working_title: $25 to move your own money
mechanism_question: Where does a $25 wire fee flow between your bank, the receiving bank, and any intermediary?
payoff: Follow a wire through correspondent banks to see who clips a fee at each hop.

working_title: Who really pays the server
mechanism_question: How does tipping reroute wage cost from the restaurant to the customer's money flow?
payoff: Tips shift payroll off the business and onto diners — a flow that lets menu prices look lower.

working_title: Taking a cut from both sides
mechanism_question: How does a marketplace route a fee flow from buyers and sellers it simply connects?
payoff: Match supply and demand, take a cut of each transaction flow — the platform owns the pipe, not the goods.

working_title: Locking in rates without locking up all your cash
mechanism_question: How does staggering CDs route a steady flow of maturing cash while capturing higher rates?
payoff: Laddered maturities keep cash flowing free periodically while most earns the higher locked rate.

working_title: Your $1,000 debt sold for $40
mechanism_question: How does a defaulted debt route from the original lender to a collector who paid pennies for it?
payoff: Lenders sell bad debt cheap; collectors profit on anything they recover — trace the resale flow.

working_title: The 3% tax on your vacation
mechanism_question: When you buy abroad, how does a 3% fee flow to the network and your card issuer on top of the exchange rate?
payoff: A purchase abroad routes an extra slice to the network and issuer — a flow most travelers never see.

working_title: A loan against your stuff
mechanism_question: Where does the money flow when a pawn shop lends a fraction of an item's value at high interest?
payoff: They lend low against collateral and earn interest — or keep the item; a two-outcome flow that always favors the shop.

working_title: A split-second bidding war for your eyes
mechanism_question: How does an ad auction route advertisers' bids into a price flow for a single impression?
payoff: Advertisers bid in real time; the winning bid flows to the platform for one view of your screen.

working_title: Reinvest, repeat, get rich slowly
mechanism_question: How does reinvesting dividends route a growing flow of new shares that pay even more dividends?
payoff: Each payout buys more shares that pay more — a self-feeding dividend flow that snowballs.

working_title: Rewards that quietly vanish
mechanism_question: How does an expiration policy let a company reclaim the reward flow it promised?
payoff: Unredeemed, expiring points let the liability flow back to the company — breakage is pure profit.

working_title: Why the biggest charge posts first
mechanism_question: How does reordering transactions change the flow of overdraft fees from your account to the bank?
payoff: Posting the largest charge first can trigger more overdrafts — a reordering that multiplies the fee flow.

working_title: Buying on the installment plan, in reverse
mechanism_question: How does layaway flow your payments to the store before you get the goods, with a fee for the service?
payoff: You fund the purchase over time plus a service fee flowing to the store — interest-free credit, but you wait.

working_title: Why creators love 'link in bio'
mechanism_question: How does a sale through an affiliate link route a commission flow back to the referrer?
payoff: The merchant pays a cut of each referred sale; trace the flow from your click to the creator's payout.

working_title: Cheap advice, at a quiet price
mechanism_question: How does a robo-advisor route a small percentage flow from assets it manages automatically?
payoff: A fraction-of-a-percent fee flows from your balance yearly — low, but it compounds like any fee.

working_title: A vacation you can't stop paying for
mechanism_question: How does a timeshare route upfront cost plus perpetual maintenance-fee flow for limited use?
payoff: A big upfront price plus never-ending fees routes a lifetime flow that resale rarely recovers.

working_title: Punished for being low on cash
mechanism_question: Where does a $12 monthly maintenance fee flow when your balance dips below a threshold?
payoff: A below-minimum balance routes a steady fee to the bank — a flow that quietly drains small accounts.

working_title: Buy low, sell high, add nothing
mechanism_question: How does a reseller capture the flow between a fixed retail price and what scarcity makes buyers pay?
payoff: Scalpers pocket the gap between list price and demand price — a pure arbitrage flow on scarcity.

working_title: Selling the recipe, not the burger
mechanism_question: How does a franchisor route a royalty flow from every location it never operates?
payoff: Franchisees pay upfront fees plus ongoing royalties — a recurring flow to the brand owner.

working_title: If trades are free, who pays?
mechanism_question: When trades cost $0, how does a brokerage route a revenue flow from order routing and idle cash?
payoff: Payment for order flow and interest on your uninvested cash route the revenue — 'free' isn't free.

working_title: Chasing points into the red
mechanism_question: How do rewards nudge a bigger spending flow that outweighs the cashback flowing back?
payoff: Points reward spending; the extra money flowing out can dwarf the rewards flowing in.

working_title: Free money with a trap door
mechanism_question: How does a 0% intro offer flow into deferred interest if you miss the payoff deadline?
payoff: The 0% window is real — but a single late or unpaid balance can route back-interest flowing from day one.

working_title: The spread you don't see
mechanism_question: Where does the profit flow when a booth buys your dollars low and sells euros high?
payoff: The buy/sell spread flows straight to the booth — the real fee hides in the exchange rate, not a line item.

working_title: The profit is the card, not the cart
mechanism_question: How does a warehouse club route most of its profit flow from annual memberships, not markups?
payoff: Goods sell near cost; the real profit flow is the membership fee paid before you buy anything.

working_title: Why savers fall behind investors
mechanism_question: How does reinvesting returns route a compounding flow that idle savings can never match?
payoff: Returns on returns build an accelerating flow; a plain savings balance grows in a straight line.

working_title: Why the jackpot isn't the jackpot
mechanism_question: How does choosing lump sum vs annuity change the actual money flow a winner receives?
payoff: The headline prize is the annuity total; the lump sum flow is much smaller after discounting and tax.

working_title: 10% off, 29% APR
mechanism_question: How does a store card trade a small discount now for a large interest flow later?
payoff: The instant discount is bait; the real flow is high-APR interest back to the issuer over time.

working_title: Why the seat next to you cost half
mechanism_question: How does an airline route different prices to different buyers to maximize the total revenue flow per flight?
payoff: Prices flex by timing and demand so the plane captures the most total money — same seat, many prices.

working_title: The menu is engineered
mechanism_question: How does menu design steer your choices to route a higher-margin flow to the kitchen?
payoff: Anchor prices and decoys nudge orders toward high-margin dishes — the flow is designed, not random.

working_title: Doubling time in your head
mechanism_question: How does dividing 72 by a rate reveal how fast a money flow doubles?
payoff: 72 ÷ rate ≈ years to double — a shortcut that shows how compounding flow accelerates with rate.

working_title: The 'free' plan with a sting
mechanism_question: How does a missed BNPL installment route a late-fee flow that erases the interest-free promise?
payoff: Miss a payment and fees flow back to the lender — the real cost hides in the penalties.

working_title: Paying to touch your own paycheck
mechanism_question: Where does the flow go when a check-cashing store skims a percentage to hand you cash today?
payoff: No bank account means a slice of every paycheck flows to the storefront — the cost of being unbanked.

working_title: You became the cashier
mechanism_question: How does self-checkout shift labor cost out of the store's flow and onto your time?
payoff: Fewer paid cashiers means payroll leaves the cost flow — the savings rarely flow back to you.

working_title: Spending your premiums before the claim
mechanism_question: How does an insurer invest the float — premiums held before claims — to earn a second profit flow?
payoff: Premiums flow in and sit as 'float'; investing it earns returns before claims flow out — profit on both ends.

working_title: Not all eggs, not all baskets
mechanism_question: How does spreading money across assets smooth the overall return flow when one piece drops?
payoff: Mixing uncorrelated assets steadies the combined flow — losses in one are offset by others.

working_title: Insuring a trip that rarely cancels
mechanism_question: How does trip insurance route a premium flow on events that almost never trigger a claim?
payoff: Low claim rates route most premium flow to profit — convenience priced well above the risk.

working_title: Who the profit flows back to
mechanism_question: How does a member-owned credit union redirect the profit flow compared with a shareholder bank?
payoff: At a credit union the surplus flows back to members as better rates, not out to shareholders.

working_title: The ticket is the loss leader
mechanism_question: How does the money flow split between studios taking most of the ticket and the theater keeping the concessions?
payoff: Studios take the lion's share of ticket flow early, so popcorn margin is what actually keeps the theater open.

working_title: Why everything wants to be a subscription
mechanism_question: How does recurring billing turn a one-time sale into a predictable lifetime flow?
payoff: Converting a purchase into a monthly flow raises customer lifetime value — predictable money beats one-off sales.

working_title: Same pizza, more slices
mechanism_question: How does a split change the share count without changing the total value flow you own?
payoff: A split multiplies shares and divides price — your claim on the company's flow is unchanged.

working_title: Betting your gadget won't break in time
mechanism_question: How does a third-party warranty route a premium flow against narrow, rarely-met claim terms?
payoff: Fine-print exclusions keep claims low so the premium flow stays mostly profit.

working_title: The quiet cut on every remittance
mechanism_question: When you send $200 abroad, how does the flow split between an upfront fee and a hidden exchange-rate markup?
payoff: Two cuts — a visible fee and an invisible spread — both flow to the transfer company.

working_title: How 2% of players pay for everyone
mechanism_question: How does a free game route its revenue flow from a tiny share of big spenders?
payoff: Most players pay nothing; a few 'whales' drive the money flow that funds the free game for all.

working_title: Going public, cashing in
mechanism_question: How does an IPO route a flow of investor cash into a company in exchange for new shares?
payoff: New shares flow to investors; their cash flows into the company (and early owners) — the first public money flow.

working_title: Five dollars here, fifty gone
mechanism_question: How do many small subscriptions route a combined monthly flow bigger than any single one feels?
payoff: Each small charge hides; summed, the recurring flow quietly drains the budget.

working_title: The nightly fee you didn't book
mechanism_question: How does a mandatory resort fee route an extra flow on top of the room rate you compared?
payoff: A separate 'resort fee' routes added cost after the price won your booking — a flow outside the headline rate.
